paper.title: RFC 7541: HPACK: Header Compression for HTTP/2, Appendix C (Examples)

program.how: written for ounce-core from the RFC's description of prefix integers, string literals, Huffman coding, the indexed and literal representations and the dynamic table with eviction; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: For all 16 examples of Appendix C (C.2.1 to C.2.4, C.3.1 to C.3.3, C.4.1 to C.4.3, C.5.1 to C.5.3, C.6.1 to C.6.3) the encoder produces exactly the published hex bytes (16 of 16)
The decoder turns the published bytes of each example into the published header list (16 of 16)

After each example the dynamic table (entries, each entry's size, and the total size) equals the published table, in the encoder and in the decoder; this includes the evictions of C.5 and C.6 with a 256-octet table (16 of 16)

The Huffman code of Appendix B (257 symbols including EOS) is complete (Kraft sum exactly 1), has no code that is a prefix of another, and each of the 256 byte values encodes and decodes back (self-consistency of the table)

expected_values_source.what: RFC 7541 Appendix A (static table, 61 entries), Appendix B (Huffman code, 257 rows) and Appendix C (header lists, hex dumps, dynamic tables); tables.inc is generated from the fetched RFC text by a script
expected_values_source.note: the Huffman code and static table are data copied as numbers, not derived. The C.2 examples fix the representation type per example (literal with indexing, without indexing, never indexed, indexed); the program's encoder is told which, and for C.3 to C.6 it uses the policy 'indexed if the whole field is in a table, else literal with incremental indexing', with Huffman coding in C.4 and C.6 only. The generator joins the one dynamic-table entry that the RFC text wraps over two lines (set-cookie in C.5.3 and C.6.3); a first version that did not made those two table comparisons fail, which was a parsing error in the generator, not in the encoder.

negative_control: built with -DNEG=1 (entry size overhead 31 octets instead of 32) the dynamic table comparison fails in 13 of 16 examples (only the three tables that are empty or unaffected still match: 3 of 16) and the program exits 1; with -DNEG=2 (Huffman padding with zero bits instead of ones) 6 of the 16 encodings differ (10 of 16 match)
not_checked: dynamic table size updates (representation 001...), table sizes changed by SETTINGS, and the decoder's error handling (invalid index, over-long integers, EOS in a string, bad padding other than as a check of the examples)
the compression ratio on real header traffic or the Huffman code's statistics
HTTP/2 itself and the other appendices of the RFC
speed (emulator run time says nothing about real hardware)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, reproduces the byte strings, header lists and dynamic-table states that RFC 7541 Appendix C publishes. It does not show that the codec is a complete, interoperable HPACK implementation.
